Maura Healey

Democratic candidate for Governor & Lieutenant Governor, Massachusetts · Incumbent

Governor of Massachusetts

Maura Healey is the Democratic governor of Massachusetts, first elected in 2022, and is running for a second term with Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll as her running mate. She officially launched her reelection campaign on January 20, 2026. Before becoming governor she was Massachusetts Attorney General.

Where Healey stands

Abortion
Supports access to abortion. In the October 15 debate she said, "I trust women and their doctors," and noted that one in three women in America live without access to abortion care.
Gas tax / cost of living
Has proposed cutting the state's 24-cent-a-gallon gas tax. Says rising costs are being driven by federal tariffs and the war with Iran.
Housing
Says her administration is working to build homes as fast as possible and has cut the time to get state permits to 30 days.
Energy
Says she stopped a developer from making taxpayers pay for a new gas pipeline and has asked for federal help to expand existing lines. Supports solar, wind, geothermal and hydroelectric projects.
Public records / government transparency
Says that if voters approve Question 1, which would put the Legislature and governor's office under the public records law, she would veto any bill that weakens it.
State Police
Backs State Police Col. Jeffrey Noble, whom she hired from outside the agency, and says swift action is taken when misconduct occurs.

Background

  • Governor of Massachusetts, 2023–present
